_comment: Library pieces whose base mesh was REMOVED on 2026-09-28 (owner decision): they had been cut from
elbolilloduro's itch.io packs, whose pages license only 'the models' and whose textures mix Textures.com / Pexels
images, so their provenance could not be confirmed to the project's standard. Each is now a PLACEHOLDER BOX of the
same size (layouts, colliders and door-clearance rules are unchanged) waiting for a real model. When you model one:
replace the mesh in library.blend (keep the collection name, the origin at the footprint centre on the floor, the
used side facing -Y, and the size unless you also update the layouts), set it in status.json, and remove its row here.
Only CC0 / MIT / public-domain or credited CC BY sources -- see assets/LICENCE_AUDIT.md.

pieces.name: Shop_Gondola
pieces.brief: A konbini gondola is 1.35-1.5 m high; 1.4 m here. Optional: a price-tag rail on each shelf lip.

pieces.name: Shop_Counter
pieces.brief: A konbini counter carries a heated hot-snack case (ホットスナック) at the customer end and a cigarette wall behind the clerk; add both. Size (1.0 m high, 0.83 m deep) is right.

pieces.name: Shop_Register
pieces.brief: Japanese POS: a customer-facing screen, a coin/change machine (自動釣銭機) and an IC-card pad; today it is a plain Western register.

pieces.name: Shop_IceFreezer
pieces.brief: The open chest freezer by the door is typical.

pieces.name: Rest_BoothSofa
pieces.brief: Booth seating as at a ファミレス; a call button (呼び出しボタン) on the table would help.

pieces.name: Gas_Pump
pieces.removed_source: elbolilloduro Gas Station pack (base mesh removed)
pieces.brief: American ground pump. Japanese stations use a slimmer ground unit with a large price panel and hoses on both faces, or, in the city, overhead units hanging from the canopy (懸垂式). Model one of each; the height (2.2 m) is kept.

pieces.name: Station_TicketGate
pieces.brief: Make it a JR/Suica gate: a slimmer body (~0.25 m), a lit IC-card pad on the top at the entry end, short flap doors, a direction light; the length 1.3 m is right.

pieces.name: Station_TicketMachine
pieces.brief: 0.8 x 0.55 x 1.8 m (券売機). Still wants a touch screen face and the fare map board above the row.

pieces.name: Station_VendingMachine
pieces.brief: 1.0 x 0.72 x 1.83 m, the Japanese drink machine. Still wants its face: sample bottles behind glass in three rows, a button row, and the take-out slot at the bottom.

pieces.name: Station_Bench
pieces.brief: Individual plastic seats on a frame, as on Japanese platforms.

pieces.name: Station_Bin
pieces.brief: Japanese station bins are sorted: a row of three (燃えるゴミ, 缶・びん, ペットボトル) with shaped openings; replace the round Western bin.

pieces.name: BusStop_Shelter
pieces.removed_source: elbolilloduro Bus Stop pack (base mesh removed)
pieces.brief: A simple shelter reads fine; Japanese ones often have a timetable panel on the side wall.

pieces.name: BusStop_Sign
pieces.removed_source: elbolilloduro Bus Stop pack (base mesh removed)
pieces.brief: The Japanese bus stop sign is a round-top plate on a pole with a heavy round concrete base and a timetable box (バス停標識).
